text:
Priya: hi everyone — first week! I'm on an M1 Mac and hitting a few weird bootstrap issues. installed asdf with brew, installed node & python, but docker-compose in projects keeps using system python and npm scripts fail. also my dotfiles symlink script errors on ~/.local/bin permissions. any quick pointers?
Theo: hey priya, welcome! :wave: common culprit is PATH ordering + how you start apps. if you installed asdf via brew ensure you source the brew path in your shell rc. what shell are you using?
Priya: using zsh. `which asdf` -> /opt/homebrew/bin/asdf. i added `. $HOME/.asdf/asdf.sh` to ~/.zshrc like the quickstart, but `asdf which node` returns the shim path while `docker-compose run web which python` returns /usr/bin/python.
Riley: docker-compose containers use the image's python, not your host. if your compose uses bind-mounts that expect host runtimes (rare), ensure the dev container image has the right runtime. For local scripts run outside containers, try `exec $SHELL -l` after editing zshrc so login/interactive startup ordering is consistent.
Priya: ah that explains the compose thing. still confused about npm scripts picking wrong node though — `node -v` in terminal shows 18.16.0 (asdf), but when running `npm run test` in VSCode it uses system node and fails on native modules.
Theo: VSCode launched from Dock won't inherit your shell login. Always open from terminal with `code .` after sourcing. Alternatively set the VSCode setting: 
```
"terminal.integrated.shell.osx": "/bin/zsh",
"terminal.integrated.shellArgs.osx": ["-l"]
```
That forces a login shell and loads your zshrc, which picks up asdf shims.
Priya: ok that fixed VSCode terminal. the dotfiles script still errors: `ln: failed to create symbolic link '/Users/priya/.local/bin/mytool': Permission denied` — the script tries to create ~/.local/bin and symlink.
Riley: check if ~/.local/bin already exists and is owned by root somehow. `ls -ld ~/.local/bin` and `stat` will show. If it's wrong do `sudo chown -R $(whoami) ~/.local` then re-run the dev-setup script (don't run the script with sudo).
Priya: i had used sudo earlier, that explains it. fixed with chown. last: REDWOOD_API_KEY access — quickstart suggests export in shellrc but i don't want secrets in dotfiles. best practice?
Theo: add a `.env.local` to project root (gitignored) and keep `.env.example` in repo with placeholders. For team secrets use 1Password: `op item get "redwood/dev/api" --fields label=password`. We also have a small helper `scripts/fetch-secrets` that injects env vars into .env.local if you have 1p CLI auth.
InfraBot: Welcome Priya! GitHub invite and internal dotfiles access granted (ticket INF-3456). JetBrains license pending.
Priya: amazing, thank you all — resolved the perms and VSCode issue. will run through the onboarding checklist and ping if anything else blocks :slightly_smiling_face:
